questions.q: What does a Dockerfile's FROM line actually determine, beyond which Linux is used?
options: Only the kernel version the host machine will run
The complete set of packages, libraries, and binaries present in the final image, which directly shapes its attack surface
Nothing by itself — all packages come from the final RUN apt install line
The CPU architecture only, with no effect on installed packages
questions.explain: FROM sets the starting package set for the whole image; every package it brings in is attack surface, whether your app uses it or not.

questions.q: What is the key practical difference between a '-slim' image like python:3.12-slim and a full distro image like python:3.12?
options: Slim images use a completely different CPU architecture
Slim images cannot run any Python code at all
Slim images still have apt and a shell, but drop documentation, extra CLI tools, and build toolchains that the full image includes
Slim and full images have identical package counts; only the compression differs
questions.explain: Slim variants are still Debian-based with apt and a shell, but trim docs, common utilities, and compilers/headers, reducing size and scanned packages versus the full image.

questions.q: What makes a distroless image like gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12 different from a slim image?
options: It has no shell and no package manager at all, removing an entire category of post-exploitation tooling
It is actually larger than the equivalent full distro image
It includes a full desktop environment for debugging
It is only available for Windows containers
questions.explain: Distroless images ship no /bin/sh and no package manager — only a runtime (or nothing, for 'static') plus whatever you explicitly copy in, so exec-based post-exploitation has no shell to use.

questions.q: Why is Alpine's small size a different kind of trade-off than distroless's attack-surface reduction?
options: Alpine images cannot be pulled from Docker Hub
Alpine still includes a shell and apk; its size comes from musl libc and busybox, not from removing a shell entirely
Alpine and distroless are two names for the exact same image family
Alpine images are always larger than python:3.12-slim
questions.explain: Alpine is small because of musl/busybox, but it keeps a shell and package manager, which distroless deliberately removes — different goals even though both end up smaller than a full distro.

questions.q: In a multi-stage Dockerfile that builds with golang:1.22 and ships gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12, what ends up in the final image?
options: The full Go toolchain, so the binary can be recompiled inside the running container
Both the golang:1.22 build stage and the distroless stage, merged into one layer
A shell is added automatically so the final image can still be debugged with docker exec
Only the compiled binary copied via COPY --from=build; the build stage and its compiler never ship
questions.explain: Only artifacts explicitly copied with COPY --from=build survive into the final stage; the build stage's toolchain, including the Go compiler, is discarded.
